_about: The Pacific war's ties (ruling 197, the offer of war: the Pacific planner's paper 12, /mnt/project-files/pacific-planner/12-the-offer-of-war.md), read by src/campaign/pacific.ts and only while the far side's switch is on. 'power' is the country the ties are written for, which begins outside both blocs leaning to 'bloc'. It counts as that bloc's co-belligerent from the month it is at war with a member of the other bloc that is at war with a member of this one, and from that month 'china', at war with it since the first day, stands with the other bloc. 'pair': when the power is at war with one of the two and the two stand together in an alliance, the other is at war with it the month after. 'with': the countries that are at war with the power the same day one of the pair is, while they stand in its alliance (its dominions are world.json's, 'follow'). 'pact': the months from which Germany and Italy are bound to the power's war with 'with' (the far-pacific-war.json event 'pact-binds'): 'book' at the stops of the history dial that keep the book, and at the others so many 'months' after 'fallen' is beaten. 'freeze': America's sales to the power (and the south's) stop on 'book' at the stops that keep the book; at the others the month after the power holds one of 'places', and at every stop the month after it is at war with one of 'wars'. Once come it does not lift. 'north': the computer's 'nat' goes to war with the power so many 'months' after 'fallen' is beaten, while the power is still at war with one of 'while', and at the stops that keep the book not before 'book'. Until then the two computers keep the peace: no great choice of either names the other. The news lines are 'says' (the freeze's are ruling 197's own words, for the countries named here). 'demand' (ruling 199(e), the planner's paper 07): Japan may demand of 'of' the ground it holds that joins 'key' by land, while the two are at peace; the computer's Japan makes it in month 'book' while the book stands in 'theatre', and where no book dates it the month after the two of 'war' go to war or 'months' after 'fallen' fell, never once 'never' is beaten. 'keepers' (ruling 199(c)): who takes a fallen country's far ground into keeping, in order, the first still fighting the victor; its forces there stay and answer to the keeper. 'shores' (ruling 200, finding 2, and ruling 202(h)): the ground whose shores the Pacific's own rows decide in place of the second front's row: the 'slice' provinces of the far side's first slice (Pearl Harbor to Dunedin: Hawaii and Alaska, Japan, China, Siam, Burma, Malaya, the Indies, Australia and New Zealand) with their cities, and any province with a coast on one of 'seas'. A staff's own landing there asks the second front's own odds and risk (open.json 'descent').

says.beside: {Power} fights beside the Axis: it is at war with {foe}, and {foe} is at war with {axis}.
says.china: {China} stands with the Allies: {power}, its enemy, now fights beside the Axis.
says.freeze: America has stopped selling oil and steel to Japan.
says.freezeBoth: Britain and the Dutch have done the same.
says.freezeDutch: The Dutch have done the same.
says.north: Three months after {fallen}'s defeat, {nat} turns east and declares war on {power}.
says.demand: {Power} demands Indochina of {of}, and Vichy gives way: Japanese troops move into Saigon and Cam Ranh Bay, and the French garrison stands down.
